verdict.rationale: Babylon.js ships llms.txt files explicitly aimed at LLM consumption, extensive first-party docs, TypeScript typings, and a large public codebase/npm footprint (234k weekly downloads) that models likely trained on; community feedback repeatedly praises documentation quality and unusually strong backward compatibility ('doesn't blindside you', 'vastly superior documentation'), which supports stable, learnable APIs. However there is no direct evidence of LLM-generated Babylon.js code succeeding on first try, some community complaints about API awkwardness/physics correctness that could trip up generated code, and docs are client-rendered without markdown mirrors (only llms.txt) which may limit scraping fidelity. Missing for 10: direct evidence of LLM code-gen success rates, confirmation that abundant third-party examples exist beyond docs/community threads, and resolution of the client-rendered-docs limitation.
